title: Model/Runtime Pinning and Cross-Version Routing Compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we iterate the runtime and onboard newer model checkpoints, customers need deterministic semantics for which model binary + runtime combo serves their requests. Currently routing implicitly maps model name -> latest compatible runtime by heuristics; this causes surprise regressions when kernel changes or quantization profiles alter generation characteristics. Goal: provide deterministic version pinning at request and route level, plus a policy-driven routing fallback that guarantees both safety (no silent incompatible pairings) and graceful degradation (controlled fallback to compatible variants).

Scope and constraints:
- Support pinning at three levels: global customer default, API request override, and per-route configuration in Console.
- Compatibility is defined as (model_version, runtime_version) tuples that have passed an automated compatibility matrix and evaluation gates.
- Fallback policies must be expressible as: strict (reject), model-variant fallback (e.g., smaller/larger quantized variant), runtime-variant fallback (e.g., previous LTS runtime), and cross-region fallback.
- Minimal API change surface: prefer configuration via existing route config + headers.
- Backwards compatible for existing customers who do not set pins.

Proposed design summary:
1) Compatibility registry: a datastore that records vetted tuples and metadata: compatibility_score, known-regressions, validated-range-of-sequence-lengths, perf-metrics. Exposed via an internal API (/compat-registry).
2) Pinning semantics: route-level config keys: default_model_pin, default_runtime_pin, allowed_runtime_range (semver set), fallback_policy (enum: "reject", "model-fallback", "runtime-fallback", "region-fallback", "best-effort"). Request headers override: X-Redwood-Model-Pin, X-Redwood-Runtime-Pin.
3) Routing decision flow (pseudocode): check request pin -> if pinned pair in compatibility registry accept -> else evaluate fallback_policy in order -> consult routing engine for available capacity -> if no compatible pair and policy==reject return 409 with guidance headers.
4) Rollout gates: new entries into compatibility registry must pass staged validation: unit tests, integration tests on canary runtime pool, offline eval on pre-defined prompt set (regression threshold), and a manual sign-off by Release Engineer for LTS channel promotions.
5) Upgrade tooling: a CLI and Console workflow that computes "compatibility delta" when runtime or model versions change, suggests safe rollout windows, and automates canary progression (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on defined SLO breaches.

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor during rollouts:
- 99th percentile latency delta relative to baseline per route
- token-level error rate (generation failures, decode errors)
- quality regression metric: prompt-set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-distance against baseline
- fallback rate (percent requests that used fallback path)
- pin-violation attempts (requests that attempted to pin incompatible pairs)

Acceptance criteria (must be met before runtime-2.4 LTS promotion):
- Compatibility registry exists and populated for top 25 models and runtimes.
- Console UI exposes route-level pinning and fallback policy controls (UX review done).
- API honors request-level pin headers and returns deterministic error when pinned pair is invalid.
- Automated canary pipeline runs and can rollback based on metric thresholds.
- Documentation and migration guide published (docs/compatibility/pinning.md).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Do we require a strict semantic versioning policy for runtimes? (pro: easier matching; con: tighter release cadence).
- How aggressive should automatic runtime-fallback be vs. preserving deterministic behavior? Current proposal favors explicitness for enterprise customers and best-effort for self-serve tiers.
